body.statement: Fix \(\mathcal A\).  If the directed part of \(H\) is acyclic and has no directed self-loop, let \(G^\star\) contain every permitted directed lag and bidirected offset, and put \(A^\star=\operatorname{an}_{G^\star}(\{X_{-\gamma},Y_0\})\).  Then \(A^\star\subseteq V\times[-\gamma-(n-1)L,0]\) and \(|A^\star|\le n(nL+1)\).  If ordinary ID on the finite ADMG \(G^\star[A^\star]\) returns \(F\), then \(F\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) and \(F(P_M)=\theta_M(y;x)\) for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\).  Failure of ID on the saturated ADMG is left undecided and is not asserted to be complete for uniform identification.
body.justification: A successful saturated ordinary-ID call gives an explicit uniform finite-cylinder functional.
body.gap: Failure of saturated ID is not proved equivalent to uniform nonidentification.
body.consumer: Acyclic EasyRCA queries can be accepted on success and otherwise abstain.
body.proof_tex:
Every directed edge of \(G^\star\) goes from time \(t-\ell\) to time \(t\) with \(0\le\ell\le L\).  Projecting a directed path in \(G^\star\) to coordinate labels gives a directed walk in the directed part of \(H\).  Because that graph is acyclic and has no directed self-loop, no coordinate can repeat.  A directed path into either query vertex therefore has at most \(n-1\) edges and total backward displacement at most \((n-1)L\).  Hence
\[
 A^\star:=\operatorname{an}_{G^\star}(\{X_{-\gamma},Y_0\})
 \subseteq V\times[-\gamma-(n-1)L,0].
\]
The interval has \(\gamma+(n-1)L+1\le nL+1\) integer times because \(0\le\gamma\le L\), so
\[
 |A^\star|\le n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}\le n(nL+1).
\]

Fix \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\), with refinement \(R\).  Exact-summary compatibility and the refinement-span condition imply \(R\subseteq G^\star\).  Since \(A^\star\) is ancestral in \(G^\star\), no directed arrow from an observed vertex outside \(A^\star\) enters it.  Removing outside observed vertices therefore leaves all structural equations on \(A^\star\) unchanged.  A pairwise exogenous root with only one endpoint remaining becomes a private root, so the marginal law on \(A^\star\) is generated by a semi-Markovian SCM compatible with the supergraph \(G^\star[A^\star]\).

If ordinary ID returns \(F\), \(\mathrm{lem:ordinary\text{-}id\text{-}soundness}\) gives
\[
 F(P_M(A^\star))
 =P_M(Y_0=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x))
 =\theta_M(y;x).
\]
The set \(A^\star\) is finite.  Thus each joint or marginal cell in the returned expression is a finite cylinder probability on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\).  Finite-alphabet marginalization uses finite sums, district factorization uses finite products, and every conditional-kernel denominator is positive by cylinder positivity.  Therefore \(F\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\).  Since \(M\) was arbitrary, the equality is uniform over \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\).  This proves only the soundness direction; an ID failure in the saturated graph is not converted into a fixed-alphabet stationary countermodel.
